assessment: This paper will be of interest to the chromosome biology field and SMC researchers in particular. The study provides cell biological, biochemical, and structural modeling evidence that a new Nse5-like protein named SIMC1 is a paralog of SLF1, and that the two compete for SLF2-Smc5/6 binding. The authors also show that SIMC1 targets SMC5/6 to polyomavirus replication centers through its SUMO binding motifs (SIMs), while SIMC1 is not recruited to DNA damage sites, supporting a specific role for SIMC1 in Smc5/6 recruitment for viral restriction.
